name: Grade 8 IIIT: App Design and Events
description: Decomposition, app purpose, users, screens, interfaces, buttons, labels, wireframes, events, screen flow, timers, user needs, variables, and test cases.

words.definition: Breaking a problem into smaller tasks.
words.example: The app idea was decomposed into screens and events.

words.definition: A person who uses an app, website, or program.
One view or page in an app.
words.example: The app had Home, Game, and Result screens.

words.definition: The controls and visual parts used to interact with a program.
words.example: The interface included buttons and labels.

words.definition: An interface element a user can click or tap.
words.example: The Start button began the activity.

words.definition: Text that identifies or explains part of an interface.
words.example: The score label showed the points.

words.definition: How a user moves between screens.
A simple sketch of an app screen layout.
words.example: The wireframe labeled every screen element.

words.definition: An action that starts code, such as a tap or timer.
words.example: A click event changed the screen.

words.definition: The path a user takes from one screen to another.
words.example: The event map showed the screen flow.

words.definition: A feature that tracks or limits time.
A named place that stores a value that can change.
Information or action the app receives.
The result shown or produced by an app.
words.example: The output was a result message.

words.definition: What users require from a design to solve their problem.
words.example: User needs affected the button labels.

words.definition: Standards used to judge whether a design works.
words.example: The success criteria described a clear app.

words.definition: A planned check to see if a feature works.
words.example: The app plan included three test cases.

words.definition: A record of planning, feedback, tests, and progress.
words.example: The logbook recorded one bug and next step.
